problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)=(4t-8){e}^{t},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.

The acceleration is zero at $t=$
{{field-1}}, and the velocity at this moment is
$v=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((4t-8){e}^{t}) \\  & =4{e}^{t}+(4t-8){e}^{t} \\  & =(4t-4){e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((4t-4){e}^{t}) \\  & =4{e}^{t}+(4t-4){e}^{t} \\  & =4t\,{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}4t\,{e}^{t} & =0 \\ 4t & =0 \\ t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t=0.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
v(0)=(4\cdot 0-4){e}^{0}=-4.
$$

Therefore, the acceleration is zero at $t=0,$ and the velocity at this moment is $v=-4.$
